analysis.title: European Fund Manager Survey: 2027: upside with constraints
key_insights: Net 67% of European FMS respondents expect European equities to rise over the next 1-3 months, up from net 44% last month and the highest since Feb '26.
Expected 12-month European equity upside is 5.92%, up from 4.53%. Expected upside to 12-month forward EPS is 6.58%, up from 6.09%.
Global investors rank Euro Stoxx third among indices expected to outperform in 2027 (19%), behind Nasdaq and MSCI Emerging Markets.
33% of European investors cite concentration in crowded trades as their biggest portfolio risk and 30% cite being underinvested. This is the crowding-FOMO tension.

Industrial Gds & Svs is the most overweight European sector for the first time since Sep '25. Construction and Healthcare moved from underweight to overweight. Basic Resources and Energy moved to neutral. BofA reads this as rotation, not broad risk-on.

High Beta is expected to outperform Low Beta by a net 17%, the highest since Aug '21. High Quality remains the strongest style preference at net 53%, and expected cyclical outperformance over defensives fell to net 30% from net 41%.

50% of investors see earnings upgrades as the most likely driver of further upside (down from 56%), followed by re-rating relative to US equities at 27%. 40% expect upgrades to be broad across sectors but concentrated in larger companies.
Cost discipline (43%) is the top expected driver of European earnings for the first time since May '26, ahead of volume/top-line growth (37%) and margin expansion (13%).

A net 40% expect European growth to strengthen, up from 22%, while a net 10% say European monetary policy is too restrictive. Geopolitical de-escalation (30%) and euro area fiscal expansion (27%) are the top catalysts for stronger growth.
A net 83% of European investors expect Europe to avoid a recession, down from 94% last month. 43% expect a higher-for-longer regime, down from 66%, and 23% expect stagflation, up from 19%.

50% of European investors name an AI investment or capex disappointment as the biggest downside risk to global growth, up from 34%. 33% see a US equity/AI valuation correction as the most likely correction catalyst.

Switzerland (net 30%) and Germany (net 27%) are the preferred European markets. France is the least preferred at net -60%, a record low. 60% name French fiscal sustainability and the 2027 election cycle as the largest political risk.
Global investors: 38% expect the Fed to hike in 2027 and 36% expect it on hold. The average expectation is for the 10-year Treasury yield to end 2027 near its current 4.9%.
A net 37% of European investors expect the ECB deposit rate to be higher in 12 months, down from 44%. A net 17% expect euro area government bond yields to be lower in 12 months.
Cash: the average cash position among European investors is 3.8%, down from 4.1%. A net 29% are overweight cash, down from 35%.
Global investors expect EUR/USD at 1.12 at end-2027, from 1.12 now. A net 38% expect the JPY to appreciate most on a trade-weighted basis, and a net 40% view the USD as overvalued.

Healthcare is picked by 23% as the best performing European sector over 12 months. Discretionary and Financials follow at 17% each. Financials are favoured despite being seen as crowded, with 27% naming Banks the most crowded theme.
33% pick AI/Technology as the most crowded European theme. European Technology is seen as the most overvalued sector. A net 20% see European equities as undervalued, up from 6%.

earnings_insights: Survey-based expectation, not a reported result: European investors expect 6.58% upside to 12-month forward EPS over the next 12 months, up from 6.09% previously.
50% of surveyed investors see earnings upgrades as the most likely driver of European equity upside, down from 56% last month.
43% see cost discipline as the main driver of European earnings, topping the answers for the first time since May '26. Volume/top-line growth is 37% and margin expansion is 13%.
50% see margin expansion through cost savings as the most likely AI impact on equities, up from 41%.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Up from net 22% previously. Survey sentiment on growth is improving even though a net 10% see ECB policy as too restrictive.
Down from 94% last month. Recession fears are rising slightly.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Versus a balanced view last month.

risk_factors: AI investment or capex disappointment: 50% of European investors name it the biggest downside risk to global growth, up from 34%, and 50% name it the biggest AI risk for European equities.
US equity or AI-related valuation correction is the most likely catalyst for a market correction at 33%.
Crowded positioning: 33% cite crowded trades as their largest portfolio risk.
French fiscal sustainability and the 2027 election cycle: 60% name it the largest political risk.
Middle East instability, including the energy and inflation channel: 53% name it the most significant geopolitical driver.
Financial event (credit event, banking stress or liquidity shock) is named the largest downside risk to global growth by 20%, and an energy price shock by 10%.
charts_described: Exhibit 32: Switzerland is the most preferred European equity market at net 30%, followed by Germany at net 27%, while France is at net -60%, a new record low.
Exhibit 41: European Industrial Gds & Svs is the largest consensus sector overweight, while Autos is the largest underweight.
Exhibit 42: European Technology is seen as the most overvalued sector.
vol_and_positioning: 33% cite concentration in crowded trades as the biggest portfolio risk, and 30% cite being underinvested.
33% name AI/Technology the most crowded European theme, followed by Banks at 27%.
High Beta is expected to outperform Low Beta by a net 17%, the highest since Aug '21.
Sector conviction, the spread between the highest and lowest sector net positioning, fell back toward its long-term average. Only seven sectors are overweight, the same as last month.
European Industrial Gds & Svs, Financial Svs and Banks are the most overweight sectors relative to history, while Autos & Parts and Media are the most underweight.
Cash positioning: European average cash is 3.8% versus 4.1% last month, and the global average is 3.6% versus 3.9%.
geopolitical: 53% of European investors see Middle East instability, including the energy and inflation channel, as the most significant geopolitical driver of markets.
Geopolitical de-escalation, including a Ukraine ceasefire, is the top catalyst for stronger European growth at 30%.
60% see French fiscal sustainability and the 2027 election cycle as the largest political risk to European markets, down from 63%.
